$comment: The data-connectors commit the managed-connector end-to-end job builds its test artifact from.
WHY A PIN RATHER THAN A BRANCH NAME. Cross-repo SHA pinning is the established convention
between these two repos, in the OTHER direction: data-connectors records a data-connect SHA in
ITS OWN .github/cross-repo-pins.json, which this repo's consumer-drift-signal.yml reads by raw
fetch from that repo's main. NOTE that no cross-repo-pins.json exists in THIS repo — the file
this pin is modelled on lives in data-connectors, so this is the same idea pointed the other way,
not an edit to an existing local file. Same reasoning applies in this direction: the job asserts
that this repo's consumer can read the artifact data-connectors' builder ACTUALLY emits, so the
producer revision has to be a fact recorded in the tree, not whatever a moving branch means on
the day CI runs. A moving ref would turn a producer-side change into a mystery failure here.
WHY THIS SHA IS A PULL REQUEST HEAD AND NOT A TAG OR main. scripts/build-connector-oci-artifact.mjs
does not exist on data-connectors' main yet — it arrives with PDP-Connect/data-connectors#97
(branch chore/publish-polyfill-connectors), which is open. That is the honest state of the world:
the producer half is unmerged, so the only revision that can build a real artifact is that PR's head.
A PR head is a legitimate pin (it is an immutable commit object, fetchable from the public repo),
but it is a WEAKER one than a merged SHA, for one specific reason: force-pushing the PR branch can
make this commit unreachable, at which point this job fails at fetch with a clear message rather
than silently testing something else. That failure mode is intended. When #97 merges, move this pin
to the merge commit on main and delete this paragraph.
THE BRANCH HAS ALREADY MOVED PAST THIS PIN, and that is deliberate rather than stale. Verified
2026-09-12: chore/publish-polyfill-connectors is at cc886056f4a146745c062e16436404b91f3abb9e,
while this pin is f8f3e91f. f8f3e91f is still fetchable (git fetch of that SHA succeeds) and its
builder produces a real oura artifact, which is what this job needs. The newer head edits
scripts/build-connector-oci-artifact.mjs (14 insertions, 12 deletions); moving the pin is a
deliberate act with a CI run behind it, not something to do blindly on branch movement.
WHY connector IS STILL oura WHEN THE PUBLISH PILOT IS ynab. data-connectors#97 changed ITS
publish matrix's pilot to ynab, and says why in publish-polyfill-connectors.yml: oura is
registered on the owner's instance but collects nothing, while ynab has 11 collecting streams
and a token credential the owner holds. That reasoning is about which connector can be taken to
REAL RECORDS end to end. It does not transfer to this job, which uses no credential and asserts
only that the artifact installs and its entrypoint imports — a claim oura supports exactly as
well. Keeping oura also keeps this job's meaning stable across the pilot change.
IMPORTANT, IF YOU CHANGE connector HERE: this key alone is NOT sufficient. The test body in
packages/local-collector/test/managed-connectors-live-registry.test.ts hardcodes the oura
connectorKey, connector_id, version and the collectOura export name; the workflow parameterises
only the BUILD and PUSH from this file. Setting connector to ynab here would build and push ynab
and then fail in the test against oura's identity. Switching pilots means editing the test too.
